stemMd: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Achterberg shows that shipping notices chosen by compositors made up most of the content of Kessling's eighteenth-century newspapers.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Achterberg argues that historians have overstated how many of the lead essays in early newspapers were actually written by the papers' editors.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Achterberg argues that the need to fit text to the page let compositors shape Kessling's newspapers more than editors did.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Achterberg found that the print shops of Kessling paid their compositors according to the number of columns they set.

explanationMd:
This passage is built around a concession followed by a claim, and the main idea is the claim. Achterberg *does not dispute* that editors wrote the lead essays; that sentence grants a point to the older view. The word *But* then introduces what she actually argues: that what readers saw on the page owed more to the compositors. The rest of the passage explains why (a page had to be filled exactly, so compositors cut, dropped and added material) and where the evidence comes from (the account books).

The option about the work of fitting text to the page giving compositors more influence than editors is the only one that states that argument and its reason. To check a main-idea answer, ask whether every later sentence serves it: the sentences on shortening letters, dropping paragraphs and adding notices are all examples of that practical work, and the account books are the evidence for it.

The tempting wrong answer is the one about being paid by the column. It is true, but it is a detail about the source Achterberg used, not the point she uses it to make.

distractorRationale.b: This misreads the concession as the thesis. Achterberg explicitly does not dispute that editors wrote the lead essays; her argument is about who shaped the rest of the page, not about how many essays editors wrote.
distractorRationale.d: This is an accurate detail from the last sentence, but it describes the account books that serve as evidence. A main idea has to state what that evidence shows, and this choice says nothing about the compositors' influence over content.
distractorRationale.a: This overstates a detail. The passage says compositors filled gaps with shipping notices, which implies notices took up leftover space, not most of the paper.

accessibilityText: Using the passage about historian Mireille Achterberg's study of print-shop account books in the port of Kessling, choose the statement that best expresses the passage's main idea.

provenance.notes: Original item. The passage opens with a concession to the view it goes on to qualify, so one distractor turns the concession into the thesis and another is a true detail about the evidence.

review.author: wave7-sat-rw-ideas-craft-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: The passage's claim is that what readers saw owed more to compositors, because a page had to be filled exactly. They cut letters, dropped paragraphs and added notices of their own choosing. C states this. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-sat-rw-run1) reached the same answer: The passage turns on 'what readers actually saw on the page owed more to the compositors', and the reason is that pages had to be filled exactly. A overstates the shipping notices as 'most of the content'. B contradicts 'does not dispute that editors wrote the lead essays'. D is a minor detail.]

review.notes: Author's own solve and uniqueness check: the claim introduced by 'But' is the thesis, and only the option about fitting text to the page giving compositors more influence than editors states it. The option about overstated editorial essays contradicts the concession; the option about payment by the column is a true detail of the evidence; the option about shipping notices overstates 'filled any gaps'. Re-solved from the stem alone with the same result. Medium: the concession-then-claim structure is the standard main-idea trap, and one wrong choice is a true detail. Not published: awaiting a blind independent solve by a second party. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
